asks.title: Bring the four core smṛtis into the index
asks.change: Kane's footnotes that quote Manu, Yājñavalkya, Āpastamba and Gautama start showing where their verse stands, on every page of the History of Dharmaśāstra that cites them.

meter.note: The four smṛtis account for up to 850 more.

proof.label: Kane's History of Dharmaśāstra, with 611 footnotes already located

basis: A vidvān for 4 months, choosing the editions and checking every match: ₹4 lakh
1 engineer-month to source, structure and index the four texts: ₹0.6 lakh

asks.title: Index the names of the Harivaṃśa: the Nāma-Kośa pilot
asks.change: The first index of names for any Purāṇic text: every person, people and place in the Harivaṃśa, verified by scholars and tied to the verse. It is the pilot for the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas. Its names are what the Purāṇa atlases need: today none of them can open a card for a person or place, as the Virāṭa Parva's can.

meter.unit: Harivaṃśa verses with their names indexed
meter.note: Up to 4,034 headwords. No Purāṇa has such an index today.

proof.label: The Mahābhārata's 13,772 named entities, from Sorensen's index

basis: 1 senior vidvān, 10 hours a month for 9 months, at ₹5,000 an hour: ₹4.5 lakh
5 junior vidvāns, 25 hours a month each for 9 months, at ₹2,500 an hour: ₹28.12 lakh
2 pāṭhaśālā students, 40 hours a month each for 9 months, at ₹400 an hour: ₹2.88 lakh
3 engineer-months for the reading tool and review queue: ₹1.8 lakh
The team is the full Nāma-Kośa's, scaled to the pilot's pace of about 1,800 verses a month.

asks.title: The Purāṇa Nāma-Kośa: an index of names for all eighteen Mahāpurāṇas
asks.change: Every person, people, dynasty and place across the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas, verified by scholars and tied to the verse, so a scholar can ask where Ambarīṣa appears, or which Purāṇas know a tīrtha, and get an answer. Released one Purāṇa at a time, after the Harivaṃśa pilot above has measured the real cost. Each Purāṇa indexed fills the empty name cards of its atlas, so a verse heard in an upanyāsam leads to everyone it names.

meter.unit: Mahāpurāṇa verses with their names indexed
meter.note: No index of names exists for any of them. About ₹20.53 lakh per 10,000 verses, so a single Purāṇa can be sponsored on its own.

proof.label: The Mahābhārata's 13,772 named entities, from Sorensen's index

basis: 5 senior vidvāns, 10 hours a month each for 3 years, at ₹5,000 an hour: ₹90 lakh
25 junior vidvāns, 25 hours a month each for 3 years, at ₹2,500 an hour: ₹5.625 crore
10 pāṭhaśālā students, 40 hours a month each for 3 years, at ₹400 an hour: ₹57.6 lakh
Half an engineer for 3 years to run the reading tool and publish each Purāṇa: ₹10.8 lakh
The Harivaṃśa pilot will measure the real pace, and the team will be set from it.

asks.title: Commission a whole Purāṇa as an upanyāsa, addressable from the first day
asks.change: A senior upanyāsakar expounds a whole Purāṇa over about a year, recorded so that every verse can be played at its own address. Priced here for a Purāṇa of average length, about 19,500 verses; a longer or shorter one scales with it, at about ₹1.87 lakh for every 1,000 verses. We begin with one adhyāya to prove the method.

meter.unit: Purāṇa verses you can hear at their own address
meter.note: About 14,600 more, if three verses in four are reached, as in the Virāṭa Parva.

proof.label: Kārtika Māhātmya, 1,094 verses already on the clock

basis: The hours come from our own series: the Kārtika Māhātmya's 1,817 verses took 25 hours of upanyāsa and the Virāṭa Parva's 2,262 took 30, about 74 verses an hour. So about 264 hours for the whole Purāṇa.
Honorarium to the upanyāsakar, about 264 hours at ₹5,000 an hour: ₹13.2 lakh (the trust sets this figure)
Recording, about 264 hours at ₹2,000 an hour: ₹5.28 lakh
Turning it into a verse-addressable edition, 264 hours at ₹49: ₹0.13 lakh (measured)
Junior vidvāns checking every verse by ear, about 528 hours (twice the recording) at ₹2,500 an hour: ₹13.2 lakh
Senior vidvāns settling what the juniors are unsure of, about 26 hours at ₹5,000 an hour: ₹1.3 lakh
6 engineer-months to build and publish the atlas as the series goes: ₹3.6 lakh

asks.title: Record the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka, with the text following the chant
asks.change: The Brāhmaṇa and the Āraṇyaka are already on the Yajurveda site with their svaras, but no one can hear them there. Vidvāns record both, and every word is aligned to the recording, as the Saṃhitā's are, so the text follows the chant.

meter.unit: hours of Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda chant with the text following word by word
meter.note: About 59 hours: 43 for the Brāhmaṇa and 16 for the Āraṇyaka. This is estimated from the length of their text against the Saṃhitā's, and the recording will measure it.

proof.label: The Saṃhitā today: the text follows the chant word by word (beta)

basis: Honorarium for the vidvāns, about 59 hours at ₹5,000 an hour: ₹2.95 lakh (the trust sets this figure)
Recording, about 59 hours at ₹2,000 an hour: ₹1.18 lakh

asks.title: Publish one out-of-print smṛti commentary
asks.change: A rare printed commentary is transcribed, indexed by its own contents, cross-linked to Kane and the index, and published free. Priced per thousand printed pages.

meter.note: The Smṛtimuktāphalam's seven volumes are the precedent. They are online in beta, still being proofread.

asks.title: Clean up and publish the Yajurveda bhāṣyas
asks.change: Sāyaṇa's and Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara's commentaries on the Taittirīya Saṃhitā are beside the text for kāṇḍas 1, 2, 3 and 6. For kāṇḍas 4, 5 and 7 they exist as typed files with gaps, and Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara on the Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka exists only as scanned pages. Each is proofread, checked by a scholar, tied to its anuvāka and published beside the text.
